concepts.def: OBAFGKM letters based on stellar spectra; correlates strongly with surface temperature.
Roman numerals I-VII labelling supergiant (I), giant (III), main sequence (V), white dwarf (VII).
Temperature of an equivalent black body radiating the same total flux as the star.
Original system devised at Harvard Observatory, ordering stars by hydrogen-line strength.
Adds luminosity class to spectral type (e.g., G2V for the Sun); standard since 1943.
Abundance of elements heavier than helium; affects opacity, evolution and population type.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordinate Systems & Time — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordinate Systems & Time brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordinate Systems & Time.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
